Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a problem by calling itself to break the task down into smaller, more manageable pieces. Think of it like Russian nesting dolls, where each doll contains a slightly smaller version of itself until you reach the smallest, solid one at the center. To prevent the function from looping forever, it must have a "base case," which is a specific condition that tells it when to stop calling itself and start returning answers. As each of those nested function calls finishes its small piece of the puzzle, the results bubble back up the chain until the original, larger problem is completely solved.
